name: Brython

attributes.attribute: a family inside the Celtic tongues uniting Welsh, Breton and Cornish
the modern arm of the P-Celtic speech
the scholar who coined the word for this family

text: Brython names a broad family inside the Celtic tongues, one that gathers Welsh, Breton and Cornish as the living heirs of the P-Celts. This family stands apart from Goidelic, the Irish arm that holds Scots and Manx speech and is often tagged the Q-Celts. Sir John Rhys invented the term Brython and its kin Brythonic to denote the Britons who kept a Celtic speech in Roman Britain. Many writers today keep Brythonic for the older base speech and reserve Brittonic for the tongues now in use. Brython remains a clear label for all that western speech and lets a reader sort it neatly from the Scottish and Irish forms.

okr.objective: Explain Brython as the family inside the Celtic tongues that unites Welsh, Breton and Cornish among the P-Celts.
